text:
maya: quick check — ran sampling for draco-13b-int6 on the longform PRD slice. unit-econ looks promising but we see a consistent recall hit on summary tasks. sharing quick numbers below.

akshay: thx. can you post the micro table and slice details? how many examples?

maya: slice=1,000 requests (avg prompt 20-60 tok). int6 vs int8: cost/token int6 ~ $0.0018, int8 ~ $0.0029. avg latency +12ms for int6. Quality (ROUGE-L, abstractive summarization): int6 -3.2 pts vs int8. For chat-style Q&A (F1): -1.1 pts.

olivia: -3.2 on summaries is large. did you try any alternative quant kernels or q8 variants? tokenization/prefix changes?

maya: only standard int6 recipe from our quant bench (per-run: kbits=6, group=128). Tried KV cache warmstart and prefix cache; no measurable lift on ROUGE. sample prompt used for slice: ```system: You are a concise summarizer. user: <long PRD>```

sam: :thinking_face: could be a distribution mismatch — maybe long-form exhibits more hallucination under int6. Can you run a 200-sample focused human eval on the worst decile?

maya: did a 200-sample human eval on the 10% worst outputs: average human delta ~4.1 pts on concision/factuality combined; examples uploaded to the eval bucket (link internal).

akshay: from product/GTN POV: consider a hybrid routing — route low-risk queries to int6 and keep int8 for risky longform. rough sim: if we route 30% of traffic (short factual asks) to int6, estimated cost saving ~22% and global quality hit ~0.5 pts.

olivia: we need reliable gating signals. suggestion: prompt tokens <50 AND expected output <100 => int6. Also use a lightweight task classifier (few-shot) to label 'summary' vs 'fact-check'.

maya: ran a gating sim using a lightweight classifier: for prompt<50 & classifier label 'factual' precision 0.88, recall 0.65. Simulation of routing with fallback (re-run on int8 when sanity checks fail) shows cost reduction 19% and keeps summary ROUGE delta to ~0.6 pts.

sam: ops questions — tail latency and variance? int6 showed higher 95p latency volatility: +40ms. any memory pressure issues?

akshay: SLA note — Dedicated customers with strict 99p latency SLO might trip. For hosted we can implement fallback logic: accept int6 answer if passes fast sanity heuristics (length, keyword-entailment, simple QA), else re-run on int8. fallback rate matters.

maya: current sanity-check fail rate on summaries ~9%. with fallback the net savings remain positive (~12% net).

olivia: recommendation draft for GTN/Product: 1) Canary: 10% traffic int6 only on low-risk routes; 2) Add fallback pipeline (int6 -> sanity -> int8 rerun) for summaries; 3) 2-week A/B with human eval on top-decile to validate. I'll draft the note and include example prompts + human-eval rubric.

sam: LGTM. @eng-runtime can we get a togglable flag to flip this on/off easily and an experiment metric for failed fallbacks?

eng-runtime: deploybot: created feature-flag `quant:ring` in the experiment service (env=staging). added metric hooks: quant_ring_fallback_rate, quant_ring_cost_savings, quant_ring_95p_latency.

maya: will start a 10% canary run tomorrow on staging and share early telemetry in the #canary-dashboard. thanks all. :rocket:
